_readme: A direct, structured transcription of the reference tables supplied with the
build brief, sourced from Indian Standards. Encoded as queryable data rather
than prose so the rules engine and the frontend read the SAME numbers - a
requirement of the brief, and the only way a recommendation shown to a user can
be traced to the clause behind it.
PROVENANCE: values are transcribed from IS 456, IS 875 (Part 3), IS 1077,
IS 2185, NBC 2016 and CSIR-CBRI guidance as presented in the reference tables.
They are quoted, not derived - unlike the 0-1 resistance ratings in
materials_seed.json, which are our own interpretation. Do not conflate the two.
GRADES: min_grade_mpa is the characteristic compressive cube strength in N/mm2
that the M-number denotes (M20 = 20 N/mm2), added so the engine can compare
grades numerically instead of parsing strings.
SEVERITY: exposure classes carry an explicit ordinal so 'at least Severe' is a
comparison rather than a lookup table of special cases.

exposure_classes.label: Mild
exposure_classes.climate_context: Fully enclosed, no rain or moisture exposure

exposure_classes.label: Moderate
exposure_classes.climate_context: Sheltered from rain, or interior with normal humidity

exposure_classes.label: Severe
exposure_classes.climate_context: Exposed to alternating wetting and drying; coastal exposure or monsoon-exposed exteriors

exposure_classes.label: Very Severe
exposure_classes.climate_context: Concrete surface exposed to sea water directly; coastal structures near the shoreline

exposure_classes.label: Extreme
exposure_classes.climate_context: Tidal zone, or direct contact with aggressive chemicals

material_recommendations.purpose: High resistance to chloride and sulphate attack

Sulphate resistance and long-term strength in marine exposure
Crack control and impact toughness under wind-borne debris loading

material_recommendations.purpose: Reduces water ingress during inundation events

material_recommendations.condition_label: Hot-humid (heat of hydration risk in mass pours)

Higher thermal mass/insulation, reduces indoor heat gain

material_recommendations.material: Fly ash, GGBS, recycled aggregates, rice husk ash (RHA)

brick_suitability.best_climate_label: Drier zones; performs worse in humid/coastal climates
brick_suitability.why: Higher water absorption accelerates deterioration in humid climates when proper mortar and protective finishes are not used. High-quality kiln-fired brick can exceed 30 N/mm2 and suits load-bearing multi-storey walls.
Low absorption prevents moisture issues, works well across India's humid-coastal to dry range, and is eco-friendly.

brick_suitability.best_climate_label: Hot or composite climates, especially mid-to-high-rise
brick_suitability.why: Lightweight with strong thermal insulation, reducing structural load.

brick_suitability.best_climate_label: Humid areas or structures exposed to moisture
brick_suitability.why: Strong and weather-resistant, ideal where moisture exposure is a concern.
Highest compressive strength (20-35 N/mm2) with very low absorption; used below ground and wherever maximum durability is needed.

masonry_properties.note: Minimum 7.5 N/mm2 required for load-bearing multi-storey masonry
Water absorption 15-20%, varying by class and firing quality
Lighter and lower load-bearing than brick; best insulation of the three
Up to 30 N/mm2 for the highest class; 15% max absorption for classes above 12.5
